Byomkesh.description: The protagonist, a renowned Bengali detective known for his sharp intellect and keen powers of observation.

Satyaboti.description: Byomkesh's wife, caring and attentive, often involved in his domestic and investigative life.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, who narrates the stories and assists in investigations.

Professor Adinath Shome.description: Byomkesh's landlord, a once-promising academic whose life is troubled by marital discord with his wife Malati Devi.

Malati Devi.description: Professor Shome's wife, known for her difficult temperament and jealousy, which causes tension in her marriage.

Ashwini Ghatok.description: The local doctor, respected for his medical skills, who is secretly in love with and eventually marries Rajani.

Mahidhar Choudhury.description: A wealthy, amiable Bengali gentleman who hosts social gatherings and is Rajani's father.

Rajani.description: Mahidharbabu's daughter, an attractive and intelligent widow who later marries Dr. Ghatok.

Nakulesh Sarkar.description: A businessman and the town's only photographer, who took the group photograph central to the mystery.

Ushanath Ghosh.description: A government official in charge of the local treasury, stern and controlling, wears dark glasses due to a glass eye.

Purandar Pandey.description: The DSP of Police, not Bengali but fluent in the language, friendly and cooperative with Byomkesh.

Amaresh Raha.description: The local bank manager, seemingly unremarkable but ultimately revealed as the criminal mastermind.

Phalguni Pal.description: A talented but impoverished and alcoholic artist, whose sketches play a role in the unfolding mystery.

Calcutta.description: A major city in eastern India, now known as Kolkata, often referenced as the place from which characters travel.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, the cultural and geographical setting for the story.

Santhal district.description: A rural area on the western fringes of Bengal, known for its indigenous Santhal population and natural landscape.

DSP.description: Abbreviation for Deputy Superintendent of Police, a senior police rank in India.

Christmas.description: A Christian festival, referenced as a time marker in the story.

New Year.description: The beginning of the calendar year, used as a time marker for events in the story.

Gujarati.description: A language spoken in the western Indian state of Gujarat, referenced in relation to Amaresh's plans.

Bombay.description: Now known as Mumbai, a major city in western India, mentioned as a possible destination for escape.

Inspector Dubey.description: A police inspector involved in the climax of the investigation.

babu.description: A respectful suffix or form of address for men in Bengal, often indicating status or familiarity.

Devi.description: A respectful suffix or form of address for women in Bengal, denoting respect or status.

almirah.description: A freestanding cupboard or wardrobe, commonly used in Indian households for storing valuables.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment for men, consisting of a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

sari.description: A traditional Indian garment for women, consisting of a long piece of fabric draped around the body.

rickshaw.description: A small, human-powered or cycle-pulled vehicle used for transport, common in Indian towns and cities.

shawl.description: A piece of cloth worn over the shoulders or head, commonly used for warmth in Indian attire.

peon.description: An office attendant or messenger, typically performing menial tasks in Indian institutions.
